title: Continuous algebraic-closure scalar extension preserves constructibility and cohomological bounds
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On profinite sets put $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, using all continuous maps, and, for each finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$, put $A_E(P)=C(P,E)$ with the restricted norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $Y$ put $B_Y=p_Y^*B$ and $A_{E,Y}=p_Y^*A_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The map $A_{E,Y}\to B_Y$ is induced by postcomposition with $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and derived scalar extension $B_Y\otimes^L_{A_{E,Y}}-$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. A module is constructible when it has finite constant local models on a finite constructible locally closed scheme stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model, def-constructible-stratification]; $\mathcal B_E(Y)$ and $\mathcal B_B(Y)$ denote complexes with bounded constructible cohomology for $A_E$ and $B$, respectively.

Let $T$ be such a scheme, fix a finite intermediate field $E$, and let $M\in\mathcal B_E(T)$. Let $r\le s$ be integers such that $H^q(M)=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$. Then
$$B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E,T}}M\in\mathcal B_B(T),\qquad H^q(B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E,T}}M)=0\quad(q\notin[r,s]).$$
More precisely, there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification $T=\coprod_a T_a$ refining simultaneous adapted stratifications of all the cohomology modules of $M$, and for every $a$ a pro-etale cover $\{W_{ai}\to T_a\}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], such that for each member there is a bounded complex $P_{ai}$ of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces, zero outside $[r,s]$, and isomorphisms
$$M|_{W_{ai}}\cong A_{E,W_{ai}}\otimes^L_{\underline E}\underline{P_{ai}},\qquad (B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E,T}}M)|_{W_{ai}}\cong B_{W_{ai}}\otimes^L_{\underline\Omega}\underline{(\Omega\otimes_E P_{ai})}.$$
Underlines denote discrete constant sheaves, acting by constant sections [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Both displayed isomorphisms are in the respective ordinary module derived categories. Empty schemes, the zero complex and single-degree intervals are allowed. No flatness of $B_T$ over $A_{E,T}$ on arbitrary modules, and no completeness of $\Omega$, is assumed.

proof.text: Work with section-ring module sheaves using [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] and [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. These statements give exact equivalences preserving the underlying sheaves, finite sums, relative tensors, K-flat complexes and derived scalar extension. Thus the cohomology and local quasi-isomorphism calculations below give precisely the specified internal-module derived objects, rather than a different coefficient category. For inverse image use [lem-sfb-internal-module-inverse-image-comparison] and [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. The coefficients are pulled back from the point, so inverse-image composition identifies the pulled-back ring with the coefficient ring on the source, naturally also for the map $A_E\to B$. Consequently geometric restriction here is exact on module sheaves and commutes with cohomology. For a morphism $h$ the derived module pullback of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] is $L(\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_h}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(h^*))$; here $\alpha_h$ is a ring isomorphism [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], so $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_h}$ is an equivalence, the composite is exact, and by the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] the derived pullback is the termwise restriction. This applies to strata and to arbitrary members of their pro-etale covers; those members need not be finite type.

source.place: Section 3, Remark 3.2 and Definitions 3.3, 3.5; explicit finite-free cycle-lifting argument for the cohomology-defined subcategory

proof.text: For each of the finitely many $q\in[r,s]$, choose an adapted finite constructible locally closed stratification for $H^q(M)$ using [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Refine these simultaneously using [lemma-constructible-common-refinement] repeatedly. Since a refinement is only a containment of sets, use concretely the scheme fibre products $Z\times_TZ'$ of strata: the projection to $Z$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (1), its composite with $Z\to T$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e), and its image is the intersection of the two images. The finitely many intersections are disjoint, locally closed and cover $T$; they are constructible since $T$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Each refined stratum maps to the strata it came from, so restriction to it factors through restriction to those strata, and base change of a pro-etale cover along it is a pro-etale cover [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The local model of a restricted cohomology module pulls back to the same scalar model, since inverse image preserves the balanced tensor presentation, or directly its finite constant-matrix presentation in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. For each resulting stratum $T_a$, take a common refinement of its finitely many trivializing pro-etale covers using [lem-weil-pbc-site-coverings-common-refinement]. Each finitely presented scalar $E$-module is a finite-dimensional vector space: a presentation makes it finitely generated, and a maximal independent subset of finitely many generators is a basis. Thus on each cover member $V$ all $H^q(M)|_V$ are finite free $A_{E,V}$-modules, say of ranks $n_q$.

source.place: Section 3, Remark 3.2 and Definitions 3.3, 3.5; explicit finite-free cycle-lifting argument for the cohomology-defined subcategory

proof.text: Choose a complex $K$ representing $M|_V$ and put $Z^q=\ker(d_K^q)$ and $H^q=Z^q/\operatorname{im}(d_K^{q-1})$. The underlying sheaf map $Z^q\to H^q$ is epic. In internal notation this follows from the kernel and cokernel constructions [lem-sfb-modobj-kernels, lem-sfb-modobj-cokernels]; the colimit hypothesis on tensor in the latter holds by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] to each of the finitely many sections of $H^q(V)$ given by the chosen bases, in the finitely many degrees $[r,s]$. Refine their lifting covers simultaneously by [lem-weil-pbc-site-coverings-common-refinement]. On every resulting member $W$ there are cycles $z_{qj}\in Z^q(W)$ mapping to all those basis sections. Since $W$ is an object of the pro-etale site of $T_a$, inverse image to $W_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ is slice restriction on underlying abelian sheaves [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] (the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] is the same left Kan extension followed by sheafification), so $z_{qj}$ are global cycles of $K|_W$ and $H^q(K|_W)=H^q(K)|_W$ has the restricted basis. This is the basis-lifting proof of Stacks Tag 08FN (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-local-lift-map), written out here rather than assuming projectivity of a free sheaf as a global object.

source.place: Tag 08FN, lemma-local-lift-map, proof by lifting finitely many basis sections; local surjectivity is Tag 03CN with Tag 00WM

proof.text: On this $W$ let $P^q=E^{n_q}$ for $r\le q\le s$, put $P^q=0$ otherwise, and give $P$ zero differential. Extend the assignment $e_j\mapsto z_{qj}$ $A_{E,W}$-linearly. Because each $z_{qj}$ is a cycle, these maps form a chain map $F\to K|_W$, where $F^q=A_{E,W}^{n_q}$ and $d_F=0$. On $H^q$ its map is the chosen basis isomorphism for $q\in[r,s]$; outside this interval both sides have zero cohomology by exact restriction and the hypothesis on $M$. Hence this chain map is a quasi-isomorphism. This constructs the local derived model, including its degree interval, rather than deducing a complex-level trivialization merely from trivial cohomology.

source.place: Section 3, Remark 3.2 and Definitions 3.3, 3.5; explicit finite-free cycle-lifting argument for the cohomology-defined subcategory

proof.text: The complex $F$ is K-flat directly: for any acyclic complex $N$, the total tensor $N\otimes F$ is a finite direct sum, over $r\le q\le s$, of shifts of $N^{\oplus n_q}$, since $F$ has zero differential. Each is acyclic and finite sums preserve the kernels and images computing cohomology. This also proves the two-sided K-flat test by symmetry. The same argument applies to $\underline P$ over $\underline E$, and to $\underline{\Omega\otimes_E P}$ over $\underline\Omega$. Therefore [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] computes $A_{E,W}\otimes^L_{\underline E}\underline P$ by $F$, and computes $B_W\otimes^L_{A_{E,W}}F$ by the zero-differential complex $(B_W^{n_q})_q$. Ordinary scalar extension of a free module is free of the same rank: the balanced maps $b\otimes(a_j)_j\mapsto(ba_j)_j$ and $(b_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j$ are inverse. Thus no tensor-exactness assertion about arbitrary $A_{E,W}$-modules enters this computation.

source.place: Section 3, Remark 3.2 and Definitions 3.3, 3.5; explicit finite-free cycle-lifting argument for the cohomology-defined subcategory

proof.text:
Let $h:W\to T$ be the composite of the stratum inclusion and the refined cover map. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization] to the actual continuous coefficient map $A_E\to B$. Its isomorphism $Lh_B^*D_{a,T}\cong D_{a,W}Lh_{A_E}^*$ has no flatness or boundedness hypothesis. By the exact restriction established in step 1 these derived pullbacks are ordinary restrictions. Together with steps 4--5 it gives
$$(B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E,T}}M)|_W\cong B_W\otimes^L_{A_{E,W}}F\cong(B_W^{n_q})_q.$$
The latter is also $B_W\otimes^L_{\underline\Omega}\underline{(\Omega\otimes_E P)}$, by the K-flat computation of step 5 and the basis $1\otimes e_j$ of $\Omega\otimes_E E^{n_q}$. The coordinate isomorphism sends $b\otimes(\omega\otimes v)$ to $b\omega\otimes v$; its inverse sends $b\otimes v$ to $b\otimes(1\otimes v)$. These formulas respect both scalar balancing relations. This proves both requested derived isomorphisms for the same $P=P_{ai}$.

source.place: Section 3, Remark 3.2 and Definitions 3.3, 3.5; explicit finite-free cycle-lifting argument for the cohomology-defined subcategory

proof.text: Write $L=B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E,T}}M$. Exact restriction and step 6 identify $H^q(L)|_W$ with $B_W^{n_q}$ for $q\in[r,s]$ and with zero otherwise. Vanishing of a sheaf on a cover implies vanishing: by [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] its restriction to each member $W$ is the slice restriction, so every section restricts to zero on that cover and the separatedness clause of the sheaf condition makes the section zero. Thus on each stratum $H^q(L)$ has finite constant local models for every $q$, and vanishes outside $[r,s]$. For such an outside degree, apply [new-det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification-exactness] to $0\to H^q(L)$: on every stratum it is epic, so it is epic globally and $H^q(L)=0$. Its hypothesis holds because $T$ is a finite-type scheme over a field, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (the only ideals of a field are zero and the whole field), and the stratification is finite locally closed. Finally [sk-def-sfb-constructible] makes each $H^q(L)$ constructible and $L$ bounded constructible. Empty strata can be omitted; if $T$ is empty the same detection statement applies to the empty family. If $M=0$ all $n_q$ and all local complexes are zero; when $r=s$ the construction has a single term. No completion of $\Omega$ or restriction on the images of continuous functions has been used.
